comparator.name: Cognition, Language and Communication
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current study-programme page specifies a complete 180-EC curriculum. Year 1 is a common 60-EC interdisciplinary foundation. Years 2 and 3 combine a 54-EC CLC core, a 30-EC bound specialisation package drawn from another programme, 30 EC of free choice and a 12-EC bachelor research project. For this generic target, Psychology is selected by the neutral first-listed option on the official programme page before comparison with UCR. The public page publishes that package only as 24 EC of bound choice in Year 2 and 6 EC in Year 3, so those aggregates are preserved rather than populated with invented course names.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target names the broad CLC programme and does not privilege one bound specialisation. Psychology is the first option listed in the official description of the second-year package and is therefore selected before UCR comparison. The 24-EC and 6-EC aggregates are retained because the public curriculum does not provide a dependable internal course split.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme-defining cognition, language, communication and empirical-research interests. Cognitive Psychology & Psychobiology and Artificial Intelligence & Cognitive Modelling are the two strongest coherent remaining generator directions and produce feasible, substantively distinct curricula. Language & Communication Studies is already covered by the closest match. Philosophy of Mind & Language and Music, Cognition & Culture are coherent but cannot be added after the maximum of three alternatives is reached. All three schedules contain 24 courses/180 EC, satisfy prerequisite and term constraints, and provide substantial 300-level depth.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce data analysis and statistical reasoning, although Amsterdam uses R explicitly.
Both develop advanced quantitative data-analysis methods.
Both use computational or artificial-intelligence modelling to test accounts of cognition.
Both develop formal and quantitative tools relevant to computational accounts of language and cognition.
Both develop qualitative research design and analysis for human behaviour and interaction.
Both connect philosophy to language, mind and cognition.
No selected UCR course is a direct counterpart to the dedicated social-interaction-and-cognition component.
Both introduce cognition through scientifically informed perspectives on mind, brain and behaviour.
Both provide a broad foundation in cognitive science and its research questions.
This advanced psychology course represents one substantive element within Amsterdam’s broader 24-EC specialisation aggregate.
Both provide advanced cognitive-psychology study within the selected Psychology specialisation.
Both develop theoretically informed analysis and practice of verbal communication and rhetoric.
Both examine persuasion and strategic communication.
Both examine advanced communication across media and modes.
No selected UCR course is a dedicated introduction to linguistic structure and theory.
No selected UCR course reproduces the dedicated critical synthesis of CLC research papers.
No selected UCR course is directly equivalent to the separately credited first-year CLC research project.
